que_es: M02 — revisión adversarial del ejecutor (workflow, preflight, verify). Tres revisores y un verificador por hallazgo que intentó refutarlo reproduciéndolo. Todos los confirmados están corregidos y tienen test (sección «Regresiones de la revisión adversarial de M02» de tests/test_m02_auto_task.py). Rutas locales reemplazadas.

confirmados.titulo: ls-remote tail matching lets a decoy branch satisfy 'TASK_COMMIT is the HEAD of TASK_BRANCH' (and the same for BASE_BRANCH)
confirmados.escenario:
remote_head() runs `git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/<b>` and takes out[0]. ls-remote matches patterns by tail, so the pattern also matches `refs/heads/+/refs/heads/<b>`, and that ref sorts before the real one.

Anyone who can create branches (Joaquin's account, or a compromised or confused ChatGPT connector) can push unapproved TASK text to `+/refs/heads/m03_smoke` and put that commit's SHA in the issue. Preflight then logs 'rama de la TASK en el commit exacto' and passes, while the real m03_smoke still shows the approved TASK, and Claude executes the unapproved one.

This violates M02 contract line 119 (TASK_COMMIT must be the expected HEAD of TASK_BRANCH) and AC6/AC7 (lines 235-236). The same trick works on BASE_BRANCH (line 243), letting arbitrary base content in under a legitimate base name.

confirmados.titulo: verify's forbidden-path filter is bypassed by git path quoting (non-ASCII, quote or backslash names) and by case variants
confirmados.escenario:
verify reads `git diff --name-only` without -z. Under the default core.quotePath, a path with non-ASCII bytes, control characters, '"' or '\' is printed C-quoted, e.g. `"src/escalimetro/\303\261.py"`. That string does not start with 'src/', so `f.startswith(FORBIDDEN_PREFIXES)` misses it.

Result: Claude can add new files under src/ (frozen engine, D-008) or tasks/, and publish pushes them. Case variants such as `Src/escalimetro/motor.py`, `SRC/...` or `Tasks/M04.md` also pass. On Joaquin's case-insensitive macOS checkout, new files under these variants land inside src/ or tasks/.

This breaks the stated invariant 'Nunca se publica algo que toque .github/, src/ o una TASK existente' (auto_task.py:28 and docs table row 4).

confirmados.titulo: Cancelling the run does not stop publication: publish uses always(), so a human cancel still pushes Claude's commits
confirmados.escenario:
Joaquin sees Claude misbehaving mid-run and presses 'Cancel workflow'. This is the only in-flight stop: deleting the secret or disabling the workflow (doc §7) does not stop a running job.

The claude job's packaging and upload steps use `if: always() && steps.claude.outcome != 'skipped'`, and the cancelled step has outcome 'cancelled', so they still run and upload impl-bundle. publish uses `if: always() && needs.gate.result == 'success' && ...`, which GitHub evaluates as true after cancellation. So publish runs, verify returns PUBLISH or PUBLISH_INCOMPLETE, and the push step creates auto/<id>-issue-<n> on the public repo.

The workflow comment (line 159) says it runs 'aunque Claude haya fallado' (failed), but a cancel is an explicit human stop.

confirmados.titulo: Two issues for the same TASK both pass preflight and run Claude concurrently; the anti-re-execution check only sees branches created at the end
confirmados.escenario:
ALREADY_EXECUTED only looks for remote `auto/<stem>-*` branches. Those are created by publish, after up to 240 minutes of Claude. The concurrency group is per issue number (workflow line 36), so nothing serialises per TASK. verify only checks that its own impl branch is absent (auto_task.py:331).

If ChatGPT opens two issues for M03 (a connector retry after a timeout, or confusion), say #7 and #8, both gates pass, both start Claude with the subscription credential, and both publish auto/m03-issue-7 and auto/m03-issue-8. Each declares itself 'base para la próxima TASK'.

This contradicts contract line 125 ('existe evidencia inequívoca de ejecución previa' must fail closed): an in-flight run of the same TASK is such evidence. It also leaves the next base ambiguous.

confirmados.titulo: Doc overstates CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB: code Claude runs can read the OAuth token on this runner
confirmados.escenario:
§8 says 'La credencial de Anthropic no llega a esos procesos (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB)', and §3 row 3 repeats it. The action's own docs/security.md:16 calls the scrub best-effort; PID isolation needs bubblewrap. Bubblewrap is installed only when allowed_non_write_users is set (action.yml:228), and runner-images Ubuntu2404 does not ship it.

Any process Claude runs via the allowed `Bash(.venv/bin/python:*)` (pytest, conftest.py, a pip-installed package's daemon) can therefore read /proc/<claude pid>/environ as the same uid, or use passwordless sudo, to get CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. The runner has open egress, and the token is valid for a year. Joaquin will decide DR-9 based on this understated risk.

confirmados.escenario: verify_impl reads 'git diff --name-only --no-renames task..head' with git's default core.quotePath=true. Any path containing a non-ASCII byte, a tab, '"' or '\' comes back C-quoted, for example '"src/escalimetro/n\303\272cleo.py"'. That string starts with '"', so f.startswith(FORBIDDEN_PREFIXES) is False and the verdict is PUBLISH. For .github/workflows/ only, GitHub's GITHUB_TOKEN 'workflows' restriction is the backstop; nothing backstops src/ or tasks/. confirmados.titulo: BASE_NOT_DECLARED is self-referential: any older chain branch is accepted as the base
confirmados.escenario: The preflight reads CURRENT_STATE.md from the BASE_BRANCH commit itself and checks that it declares BASE_BRANCH. In this repo every finished branch declares itself as 'base para la próxima TASK': origin/e37_reconstruction_lab and origin/m01_1_remote_truth do today, and m02_github_executor will once M02 is committed (working tree line 33). So a TASK branch cut from a superseded base (m01_1_remote_truth, which is an ancestor of e37_reconstruction_lab) passes, and Claude executes an approved TASK on stale code. This violates M02 line 107 (BASE_BRANCH = the base CURRENT_STATE declared when the TASK was created) and AC1 line 230 ('base correcta'). It is exactly the case the new tests/test_ai_handoff.py docstring says must not happen: 'una rama vieja se aceptaría como base'. It also makes the declared-base parsing tricks (first matching row wins, rows inside code blocks count) irrelevant, beca

confirmados.titulo: The same TASK can run twice: per-issue concurrency, and no re-check of auto/<id>-* at publish time
confirmados.escenario: The concurrency group is escalimetro-auto-task-<issue number>, so two issues for the same TASK run in parallel. The preflight's ALREADY_EXECUTED check (auto_task.py:272) only sees branches that have already been published. A run can last up to 240 minutes, so a second issue opened at any point before the first one publishes passes the preflight, starts a second Claude run (a second OAuth spend), and publishes a second implementation branch. verify (auto_task.py:331) checks only its own impl_branch name, not other auto/<stem>-* branches. Each resulting branch has a CURRENT_STATE declaring itself as the next base, which the self-referential base check then accepts. This violates M02 line 44 ('ejecute exactamente una TASK aprobada') and line 125 (prior execution must fail).

confirmados.titulo: remote_head uses ls-remote suffix matching, so a moved TASK branch can pass (AC7)
confirmados.escenario: git ls-remote treats each pattern as '*/<pattern>' (a tail match), and remote_head returns the first output line. If any head named '<x>/refs/heads/<task_branch>' exists and sorts first, its SHA is used. After the issue is created, someone moves m99_prueba to a revised commit (for example one revoking the TASK) and creates 'a/refs/heads/m99_prueba' at the old TASK_COMMIT. The preflight then returns PASS instead of TASK_BRANCH_MOVED, which violates AC7 (line 236) and lines 119 and 126. The same shadowing can substitute the BASE_BRANCH SHA. This needs a writer to create an oddly named ref; the code Claude runs is still the TASK_COMMIT the preflight validated. On a valid push the impl_branch lookup in verify only fails closed.

confirmados.titulo: The 'Decisión aprobada' check reads the LAST heading with that name, including headings inside code blocks; comment-only content also passes
confirmados.escenario: _sections splits on '^##' everywhere, including inside fenced code, and builds a dict where later duplicates overwrite earlier ones. A TASK whose real 'Decisión aprobada' section is empty, but which quotes the TASK template from DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL.md §6 (line 162 contains '## Decisión aprobada' plus text), passes NOT_APPROVED. A section holding only '<!-- pendiente de aprobación -->' (invisible on GitHub) or only '### (pendiente)' also passes. This violates M02 line 124: a TASK that does not declare approval must fail closed. The issue-opener actor gate still applies.

confirmados.titulo: verify's forbidden-path check (.github/, src/, tasks/) is bypassed by git quotePath for non-ASCII or special-char filenames
confirmados.escenario: verify_impl lists changed files with `git diff --name-only` using git's default core.quotePath=true, then runs `f.startswith(FORBIDDEN_PREFIXES)`. Git prints names with non-ASCII bytes, '"' or '\\' quoted with a leading '"' (for example "src/escalimetro/a\303\261o.py"), so the prefix test never matches. A Claude commit adding src/escalimetro/año.py, tasks/M99ñ.md or .github/workflows/ñ.yml gets verdict PUBLISH and the publish job pushes it. This breaks the guarantee in AUTO_TASK_EXECUTOR.md §3 row 4 and D-012 ('lo publicado no puede tocar .github/, src/ ni tasks/') and the D-008 src/ freeze; for workflows only GitHub's missing `workflows` permission still protects (M02.md:163-164).

confirmados.titulo: The same TASK can run (and publish) twice: concurrency is per issue and verify checks only its own branch name
confirmados.escenario: The concurrency group is `escalimetro-auto-task-${{ github.event.issue.number }}`, so two issues for the same TASK run in parallel. The preflight's ALREADY_EXECUTED check only looks for remote `auto/<id>-*` branches, which exist only after publish. The claude job can last up to 240 minutes. A second issue opened in that window (a retry, or ChatGPT opening it twice) passes preflight, runs Claude again (a second paid run), and publish creates a second branch: verify_impl (auto_task.py:331) only rejects if its own `auto/<id>-issue-<n>` exists, not any `auto/<id>-*`. The result is two implementation branches for one TASK, each declaring itself the next base. This contradicts M02.md:125 (fail closed on evidence of prior execution) and M02.md:44 ('exactamente una TASK aprobada').

confirmados.titulo: Cancelling a run does not stop publication: the bundle, upload and publish steps use always() instead of !cancelled()
confirmados.escenario: The steps 'Empaquetar' (line 143) and 'Entregar el bundle' (line 149) use `always() && steps.claude.outcome != 'skipped'`, and the publish job (lines 160-164) uses `always() && needs.gate.result == 'success' ...`. GitHub runs always() steps and jobs even when the run is cancelled. If Joaquín cancels a misbehaving run mid-execution (the obvious stop control for a 'mecanismo ... revocable', M02.md:44), the cancelled Claude step's partial commits are still bundled, uploaded, verified as PUBLISH_INCOMPLETE and pushed to auto/<id>-issue-<n> on the public repo. That branch then makes every later issue for the TASK fail with ALREADY_EXECUTED. AUTO_TASK_EXECUTOR.md §7 ('Cómo se apaga') does not mention this.

confirmados.titulo: The YAML gate tests are substring-only, so turning the gate conjunctions into disjunctions still passes every test
confirmados.escenario: test_la_compuerta_corre_antes_de_cualquier_secreto and test_claude_corre_sin_poder_escribir_y_solo_si_paso_la_compuerta only assert that each condition string appears before runs-on:. They do not check the boolean structure. AC4 and AC8 (M02.md:233, 237) are therefore evidenced only by the presence of the conditions, not by the condition actually rejecting anything. Today the preflight's check_actor is a second layer, but the tests would not catch a regression in the first one.

confirmados.titulo: The issue comment announces the branch whenever verify said PUBLISH, even if the push failed
confirmados.escenario: 'Informar en el issue' runs with if: always() and prints 'Rama: https://github.com/.../tree/<impl>' based only on VERDICT. When the push step fails (GITHUB_TOKEN rejected for a workflow file, a ruleset on auto/**, a race, a network error), the comment still points ChatGPT, which audits from GitHub, at a branch that does not exist. Only the run status shows the failure.
